clue.text: Mineral carried by artist in case

indicators.note: the artist's letters sit in the middle of the word for a case

parts.note: a box is a case for holding things
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter keeps a mineral specimen packed in a carrying case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' is just link wording; the container signal is 'in', putting RA inside BOX.
explanation.definitionFit: Borax is a white crystalline compound mined as a natural deposit, used in cleaning products.

clue.text: Little Edward has nice work — that'sheavenly…

parts.note: Ed is the short form of the name Edward

indicators.note: the letters of nice are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A small boy called Edward does a lovely job, and it seems divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges NICE into ENIC, placed after ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden was paradise, so anything like the Garden of Eden is blissful and divine.

clue.text: … an excuse, without doubt, for happiness

parts.note: a plea is an excuse offered in defence
sure means certain, free of doubt

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a heavenly feeling gives an excuse for being happy.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening dots link this clue to the one before for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or delight, a close synonym of contentment and joy.

clue.text: Stupid as one having one over the eight

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
one more than eight is nine

explanation.surface: Someone who has had one drink too many behaves foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is a British idiom for being slightly drunk, which hides the plain arithmetic of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means like an ass, foolish and silly.

clue.text: Form of sea-life not served up on board

indicators.note: in a down clue the turned word sits on top of, that is after, the board

parts.note: a plank is a long board of wood

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the word not is written upwards, so back to front

explanation.surface: Something from the sea is not presented on the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses NOT to TON, which follows PLANK in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are the tiny drifting organisms that float in seas and lakes.

clue.text: Let air in a system, among other things

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new system, an arranged order

explanation.surface: Instructions to ventilate a system, mentioned among various items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'system' rearranges the nine letters of LET AIR IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is Latin for amongst others, used to list a few examples.

clue.text: Not a troublesome form of commendation

definitions.text: Not a troublesome form of commendation

parts.words: Not a troublesome form of commendation
parts.note: a school form that is well behaved, read as words of praise

explanation.surface: A school report praising a well-behaved form.
explanation.definitionFit: Good class is a phrase of approval meaning of high quality, while also suggesting a well-behaved school form.

clue.text: Smooth beginner in the ensemble

indicators.note: the beginner's letter is put inside the group of musicians

parts.note: a band is a musical ensemble
L stands for learner, a beginner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A novice musician playing in the group sounds suave.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland means mild and soothing, without harshness; smooth in manner.

clue.text: Sounds topping for the old party

indicators.note: the clue says what is heard when the word for topping is said

parts.note: a wig is a hairpiece worn on top of the head

explanation.surface: A hairpiece sounds fine for a historic political party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whigs were a British political party, forerunner of the Liberals.

clue.text: Support by argument

definitions.meaning: to keep up or provide for
to assert or uphold a position in debate

explanation.definitionFit: To maintain is to keep something going, and also to insist a claim is true in debate.

clue.text: Watch for one who follows the game

definitions.meaning: a pocket timepiece with a hinged cover

explanation.definitionFit: A hunter is a pocket timepiece with a protective lid, and also a person who chases quarry.

clue.text: Colour section of the cruise brochure

indicators.note: only a section of the words the cruise is taken, the run straddling them

explanation.surface: A colour picked out of part of a holiday cruise brochure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow or beige shade, like unbleached linen.

clue.text: Sort of thing to shock this summervisitor

definitions.text: Sort of thing to shock this summervisitor

parts.words: Sort of thing to shock this summervisitor
parts.note: a jolt in the dark is split as two words, naming a bird that visits in summer

explanation.surface: Something that startles a seasonal visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: A jar is a shock, and one at night gives the bird's name; it is a migrant that visits Britain in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird that migrates to Europe for the warmer months.

clue.text: Solo effort, one may say

parts.note: a speech made by one performer alone, said with a pun on mono as single

explanation.surface: Someone doing a task alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A monologue is a long speech by one person alone, as in a play.

clue.text: Two take time for a bit of verse

parts.note: a couple is a pair, two

explanation.surface: A pair takes a while over writing some poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of rhyming lines in poetry.

clue.text: private book

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'private book (8)' looks cut short; no scan, and the wordplay for the answer cannot be recovered from it.

clue.text: He takes one's foreign money for a start

indicators.note: the money word takes the letter for one into it

parts.note: francs were the currency of France and other countries
I is one; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A man exchanges his currency abroad before starting a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a start' hints that the answer is a first name, the start of a man's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis is a man's first name, so it stands for a male person.

clue.text: How Don Quixote faced the world, we're told

definitions.text: How Don Quixote faced the world, we're told

parts.words: How Don Quixote faced the world, we're told
parts.note: Cervantes calls his hero the Knight of the Sorrowful Countenance, so he faced things with a sad face

explanation.surface: A remark about the attitude of Cervantes's knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruefully means with regret or sorrow, matching the knight's mournful countenance.

clue.text: The old convict gets a flier

parts.note: grey-haired, so old
an old lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: An elderly prisoner gets on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a wild goose, a bird that flies in long migrations.

clue.text: In concert to win the lady

parts.note: to get is to obtain or win
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A suitor sets out to win a woman's hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In concert means jointly, with others at the same time.

clue.text: Covering English antipathy

parts.note: a hat is a covering for the head

explanation.surface: A dislike for something wrapped in English style.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate is intense dislike, a strong aversion.

clue.text: Trees of note on the old railway system

parts.note: E is a musical note
the LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway

explanation.surface: Notable trees growing alongside a former railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The LMS was one of the big four British railway companies before nationalisation in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: Elms are large deciduous trees with serrated leaves.

clue.text: Cat circles round a child's horse looking for grub!

indicators.note: the turned cat goes round the other letters, holding them inside
the cat word circles back on itself, turning around

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
gee-gee is a nursery word for a horse

explanation.surface: A cat prowls around a rocking horse hunting for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' turns TOM into MOT; 'round' puts A GG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is the larva of a fly, a type of grub.

clue.text: Crazy as one can get from an iced drink

indicators.note: the answer can be extracted from within the words from an iced

explanation.surface: Someone acts wildly after drinking something very cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic means frenzied and wildly excited, as if mad.

clue.text: Dissipating advice to youth?

parts.note: a famous call to young men to move to the frontier, while going west also means vanishing

explanation.surface: Counsel to youngsters that might lead them astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase, linked to Horace Greeley, urged young Americans to head for the frontier; to go west is also slang for being lost or ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying urged young Americans to head for the frontier, and going west is slang for vanishing or wasting away.

clue.text: See 25
At tea-time the parish priest goes round the bend

indicators.note: the priest's word encloses the tea-time letter

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
five o'clock is tea-time, and V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Around tea, the local vicar goes mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea-time is traditionally five o'clock in Britain, hence V.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve is a bend in a road or line.

clue.text: Be taken in on the trip?

definitions.text: Be taken in on the trip?

parts.words: Be taken in on the trip?
parts.note: being fooled, read as tumbling over while tripping

explanation.surface: Getting fooled during a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall for it is to be deceived by a trick or ruse.
